sources.quote:
V7: six-snapshot reference reproduction and correlated comparison

Sources and execution
Source data: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/michellab/EMLE_HFE_SI/0279424ec1770e155533af6247f28ebca98b72b5/data/testing_datasets/testing_data_iter1.pkl
SHA256: 4328e00ac747df3609ec72dedf5a82c5acba539ebbec5fe5f97aee9a00956235
Existing evidence is reused read-only from emmy/review1. The source hash is asserted before restricted reading.
Only the four NumPy globals previously opcode-audited in entry 42 are permitted.
Scripts are outside the data directory, in ada/review2, and run with Python -I.
Isolated uv environment: Python 3.12.13, PySCF 2.14.0, NumPy 2.5.3, SciPy 1.18.1, h5py 3.16.0, LibXC 7.0.0.
The macOS PySCF wheel reports no OpenMP; effective PySCF thread count is 1 despite requesting 2.
Commands: venv/bin/python -I reference_audit.py --method b3lyp5
          venv/bin/python -I reference_audit.py --method b3lyp5 --level 5 --record 4
          venv/bin/python -I reference_audit.py --method mp2 --tight
          venv/bin/python -I tabulate_audit.py
Paths in these commands are relative to ada/review2. Exact executable source is reference_audit.py.
Outputs include each run's energies, timings, convergence choice and decomposition; provenance.json hashes scripts/results.

Selection and units
Each molecular composition has 100 records. Indices are zero-based global pickle indices.
Within each formula group choose the observed induction nearest its median, 1st percentile and 75th percentile.
Water: 1912, 1926, 1951. Methanol: 935, 909, 992, respectively.
These are deliberately selected records, not random draws or an unbiased ensemble.
Coordinate distances support Angstrom units: nearest H-O distances 0.9452 to 1.0056.
Every retained MM atom has a nearest-solute distance below 12 Angstrom, matching Q's atomwise cutoff.
The truncated MM charge sets have nonzero net charges; no neutralisation, recentering or new cutoff is applied.
Record geometries and charges are saved in selected-records.json; geometrical checks are in input-geometry-checks.json.
Labels are kJ/mol, as established by the author notebook conversion in entry 42; report tables use kcal/mol.
Hartree conversion used: 2625.4996394799 kJ/mol. No MM self-energy or LJ energy is included.

Decomposition and nuclear conventions
At fixed geometry define \(H(s)=H_0+sV\), where the MM charges multiply by physical perturbation strength \(s\).
PySCF qmmm includes both electronic attraction and the solute-nuclear/MM scalar in total energy.
Official implementation description: https://pyscf.org/pyscf_api_docs/pyscf.qmmm.html
The static term is \(D=\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma_0 v_{\rm MM})+N_{\rm MM}\).
The induced term is \(I=E(1)-E(0)-D\), following Q eq16, primary ada/Q-accepted-layout.txt:615-637.
Electronic-only convention uses \(D_e=D-N_{\rm MM}\) and \(\Delta E_e=E(1)-E(0)-N_{\rm MM}\).
Thus \(\Delta E_e-D_e=I\): consistent removal cancels from induction.
Removing nuclear electrostatics only from static while retaining total embedded energy is inconsistent and fails badly.
reproduction.csv:2-7 contains labels, both static conventions, both consistent induction conventions and residuals.
The static labels clearly include nuclear electrostatics: electronic-only values range -1644.64 to +482.02 kcal/mol,
whereas matching total static values range -34.10 to -9.96 kcal/mol.
This pins down these records' decomposition convention, not all production simulation conventions.

DFT reproduction
Basis: spherical cc-pVTZ, all atoms and retained point charges, neutral singlets, no density fitting, no frozen orbitals.
Predeclared reproduction tolerance was 0.02 kcal/mol per component (entry 70); all six pass.
Default PySCF b3lyp also passes but is the VWN-RPA/Gaussian variant, not ORCA's default VWN5.
ORCA manual: https://www.faccts.de/docs/orca/6.1/manual/contents/modelchemistries/DensityFunctionalTheory.html
PySCF explicit b3lyp5 definition: https://pyscf.org/_modules/pyscf/dft/libxc.html
Use b3lyp5 for the component comparison. Static residual range -0.004936 to -0.000230 kcal/mol;
induction residual range +0.000966 to +0.004493 kcal/mol. Maximum residual is below 0.005.
PySCF grid level 4; SCF energy tolerance 1e-11 Hartree. Strong methanol grid level 5 check changes
static by -0.000001821 and induction by -0.000000188 kcal/mol, much smaller than label residuals.
Original ORCA grid, exact version, possible integral approximations and generating scripts remain unavailable.
Residuals are therefore not attributed solely to grid or functional differences; this is tolerance reproduction.

Correlated follow-up
MP2 with RHF orbitals uses full cc-pVTZ and all electrons, at unchanged geometry and point-charge field.
Official method documentation: https://pyscf.org/user/mp.html
Static term comes from relaxed total-energy response: \(D_h=[E(h)-E(-h)]/(2h)\).
No unrelaxed MP2 density is substituted for the derivative. Induction is again \(E(1)-E(0)-D_h\).
Use \(h=0.0005\), checked against \(h=0.001\); tightened SCF energy tolerance 1e-13 Hartree and gradient 1e-9.
Step-size discrepancy is below 0.00000081 kcal/mol for every record.
An initial less-tight run for water 1951 differed by about 0.00146 kcal/mol in the derivative;
the tightened rerun resolves this and its raw initial output is preserved.
correlated-differences.csv:2-7 gives MP2 values, MP2-minus-B3LYP5 static/induced/total changes and step-size checks.
Water static shifts: -0.3263, -0.6206, -0.3842; induced shifts: +0.0960, +0.1835, +0.0728 kcal/mol.
Methanol static shifts: -0.4573, -0.4821, -0.1121; induced shifts: +0.0745, +0.1112, +0.0302 kcal/mol.
All selected total electrostatic shifts are negative, ranging -0.4371 to -0.0820 kcal/mol.
Static and induction shifts oppose each other; a response-only reference replacement misses this feature.

Scope
MP2 establishes a nonzero correlated-versus-DFT reference change for these records, not improved physical accuracy.
No higher-order correlated-method convergence, complete-basis convergence, solvent back-polarisation or spill-out audit is claimed.
A handful of selected snapshots is not an ensemble result, hydration prediction, quantum calculation or quantum-cost result.
Do not extrapolate these changes to Q's 0.6 empirical scaling or the hydration bias.
Compare with EMLE fit residuals only descriptively, and retain static-density/LJ alternatives and ensemble requirements.
The narrow next question is response-certified selection at identical physical Hamiltonians and fair total cost.
No scientific verdict on double counting, publication novelty or quantum advantage is assigned.
